title: Hosted API: embeddings + rerank demo - Search relevance walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked NovaSearch through Hosted API embeddings + reranking flow. Showed embedding creation, vector search integration, then a two-stage rerank using Redwood's rerank endpoint. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, batch/kv caching, and data residency/SOC2. Agreed to send pilot pricing, security pack, and schedule POC scoping next week.
next_steps: Alex to send pilot pricing and example billing scenarios
Priya to share reranking notebook and sample benchmark scripts
Send SOC2 and security docs (Redwood security pack)
Schedule POC scoping meeting for week of Dec 14
action_items: Alex Chen: send pilot pricing and integration checklist (due 2026-12-13)
Priya Natarajan: upload rerank notebook and sample requests (due 2026-12-12)
Samir Patel: share representative query log and top-1000 doc sample (due 2026-12-14)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-10
- Time: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (NovaSearch), Li Wang (Eng Mgmt), Aisha Gomez (Product)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm alex, i'm the account lead here at Redwood. priya's our solutions engineer, she'll do the demo and run through the rerank flow.
[00:08] Samir Patel: thanks alex. excited to see this, we are specifically looking at improving our search relevance for the help center + docs. latency target is sub-200ms on the re-rank step ideally.
[00:18] Priya Natarajan: great, thanks samir. quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, how you'd plug into your ANN store, and then our rerank endpoint which takes the top-k and re-scores them with a LLM based reranker. we'll also cover cost/latency tradeoffs and security questions. sound good?
[00:30] Li Wang: yes, go ahead. also curious about throughput — we see spikes around 400 qps during releases.
[00:36] Priya: got it, we'll cover batching and autoscaling.
[00:40] 
[02:12] Priya: ok jumping into the hosted api — here is the embeddings endpoint. you POST text, get back a vector. note we have model catalog — for retrieval we usually recommend the emb-2-small or emb-4-high depending on recall/latency. emb-2-small is faster and cheaper, emb-4-high gives better recall.
[02:28] Aisha Gomez: what is typical vector dim? are these compatible with faiss/pinecone?
[02:33] Priya: vectors are 768 or 1024 depending on model, and yes they're standard float32 arrays so compatible with FAISS, Pinecone, Milvus, etc. a few customers quantize for storage but we recommend keeping float32 for rerank quality.
[03:05] Samir: our stack today uses Elasticsearch with a plugin for ANN and a small re-ranker service that's homegrown. we want to replace the reranker with a hosted rerank to reduce ops.
[03:20] Alex: that's a common pattern — initial ANN recall in your existing store, then call Redwood rerank for top-10/50. you get a better ordering and can include context like user signals.

[05:00] Priya: demo time — i have a notebook. first step: generate embeddings for a document corpus. here's an example request, note the batching and the streaming for long lists. (small pause) transcription glitch: i said straeming earlier — meant streaming.
[06:10] Priya: next, index those vectors in your vector DB. then at query time you do knn to get top-k. we pass those doc candidates to our rerank endpoint: it's a POST with query, candidates, and optional metadata. it returns scores and a re-ranked list.
[07:00] Li Wang: how many candidates do you usually rerank? top-10? top-50?
[07:05] Priya: typical is top-10 or top-20 — top-50 sometimes for complex queries. cost scales linearly with candidates, and latency depends on model and sequence length. we suggest a two-stage approach: use a cheaper embed model for recall and a mid-sized rerank model for quality.
[07:40] Samir: is the rerank call synchronous? we need under 200ms for the critical path.
[07:48] Priya: yes it's sync, we have low-latency variants tuned for reranking — they hit ~80-150ms P95 for top-10 on our hosted infra for the mid model. you can trade cost for latency by choosing smaller models or enabling prefix caching.

[12:10] Priya: quick aside on caching — Redwood has prefix / KV caching for repeated queries and we also do automatic batching to improve throughput. if you have stable query patterns during a release spike, caching can reduce calls to the rerank model substantially.
[12:40] Li Wang: do you support client-side caching or is that server-managed?
[12:44] Priya: server-managed caching inside the runtime; we expose TTL controls and you can pin what gets cached via the console.

[15:30] Priya: security — for hosted api we offer encryption at rest, in transit, SOC2, and enterprise contracts can opt-in to private deployments. we integrate with customer KMS for dedicated/private.
[15:55] Samir: we need SOC2 + SSO + audit logs and the ability to keep logs for 12 months.
[16:02] Alex: all standard for our enterprise tier; we'll send the security pack after this call.

[18:22] Priya: back to demo — showing a live example: query "how to reset password" returned top docs, then reranked by relevance. you can see the score deltas; often the reranker pushes docs that contain explicit procedural steps higher.
[19:10] Aisha: can we include user click data / personalization signals in the rerank?
[19:15] Priya: yes you can include arbitrary metadata per candidate (user recency, click_rate) and the reranker model can condition on those. just note privacy constraints — if those signals are PII you should consult the security pack and possibly use private deployment.

[22:50] Samir: what about throughput — those 400 qps spikes. how does Redwood handle autoscale?
[22:58] Priya: for hosted we autoscale pools, and we recommend a small warm reserve for predictable spikes. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools. for your 400 qps pattern we can size reserved capacity or rely on quick autoscale with burst options.
[23:25] Li Wang: price estimates?
[23:28] Alex: we'll send a few pilot scenarios — per-embedding cost, per-rerank call cost (based on candidate count and model size), and a committed-Dedicated option. i'll include example math for your qps patterns.

[28:00] Priya: note about metrics and observability — the console gives token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and tracing hooks so you can see where time is spent between ANN lookup and rerank.
[28:20] Aisha: can we ingest logs into our datadog?
[28:25] Priya: yes via our webhooks and syslog forwarder; we also provide S3 exports for raw traces.

[31:12] Priya: demo: running a benchmark. we reranked top-10 for a 1k query sample, P95 latency ~130ms with rerank-mid model. for top-20 it went to ~180ms. cost per call was~ $0.015 for mid model; these numbers of course are illustrative.
[31:45] Samir: that looks promising. our current internal reranker is 120ms P95 but costs more to maintain.

[35:00] Alex: some implementation notes — simplest path: keep your ANN in place, use a batch job to generate embeddings for all docs, then at query time call embed->knn->rerank. we can also help with a small POC to validate metrics.
[36:10] Li Wang: curious about data residency — our EU customers require data never to leave the EU.
[36:18] Alex: hosted supports regional controls; for strict residency we can use private deployment in a VPC or an on-prem package. we'll include options in the security pack.

[39:02] Aisha: any common gotchas?
[39:06] Priya: two common ones: sending long context to rerank increases latency — we recommend truncating to the best candidate snippets; and re-ranking too many candidates increases cost linearly. also ensure your embedding model and rerank model are aligned in tokenization.

[42:30] Priya: ok wrap up — recap: we'll send pilot pricing, the security pack (SOC2, SSO info, audit logs), and a rerank notebook + benchmark scripts. we propose a POC scoping meeting next week to size dedicated capacity vs hosted pilot.
[42:50] Samir: perfect. i'll gather a sample query log and share it.
[43:00] Alex: thanks all. can we pick a time for the scoping meeting? how's Dec 15 or 16?
[43:10] Li Wang: Dec 15 works for us.
[43:15] Alex: great. thanks again, bye.
[43:20] Samir: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'straeming' / 'streaming'), speaker overlap near end.
